messages:
maya: Heads-up — we're seeing a regression in tail latency on canary after the runtime merge from yesterday. p95 jumped ~120ms on short sequences, p50 ~+30%

sam: saw the alert. CI perf job flagged compile-queue depth peaking and a bunch of kernel compile failures (OOMs) during the same window.

infra-bot: Alert: compile-queue length = 218 (threshold 80). rolling window: 5m.

liam: throwing profiling output here — looks like kernel selector keeps oscillating picks between kernel A and kernel B for the same op shape, triggering repeated JIT compilations. logs: 
```
KERNEL_SELECT: op=matmul seq_len=64 batch=2 candidates=[A(7.2ms),B(6.9ms)] chosen=B
COMPILE_START: kernel=B v=1
KERNEL_SELECT: op=matmul seq_len=64 batch=2 candidates=[A(7.1ms),B(7.05ms)] chosen=A
COMPILE_START: kernel=A v=1
COMPILE_QUEUE: enqueue kernel=A
COMPILE_QUEUE: enqueue kernel=B
COMPILE_QUEUE: depth=120
```

liam: the diff in measured latencies is within noise, so heuristic is flipping on tiny deltas (no hysteresis/TTL).

anya: can we bisect to the chunk that touched selector heuristics? I think there was an autotune change in #4251 that removed sticky_ttl=30s.

sam: starting bisect now. quick note: canary region 3 shows worst effects because compile concurrency is lower there.

maya: CI perf job output snippet: p50_tokens_ms: baseline=12.4 new=16.1 (+29.8%), compile_queue_avg_latency_s: baseline=0.3 new=2.1, compile_failures=12.

deploy-bot: Deploy 2026-03-18T09:12:03 started (canary).

sam: bisect point found: merge 6a7f9d (autotune: remove kernel selection hysteresis) correlates exactly with jump. reverting locally reduces queue depth and p50 drops back.

maya: thanks. that's a pretty clear signal. but we need a less risky fix than full revert — propose reintroduce hysteresis with small TTL and bump eval sample window to reduce noise sensitivity.

liam: agree. patch idea: add sticky_ttl=60s per op-shape + require measured delta > 5% AND 2-sample confirmation before switching. I'll draft patch.

anya: does that interact with cold-start compile storms where sticky ttl could keep a bad kernel pinned? we should have an escape: allow immediate switch if compile failure/error counts increase > X.

liam: good call. add emergency fallback: if chosen kernel causes >=3 consecutive errors or slowdowns > 40% compared to expected, bypass ttl for one decision and mark candidate as degraded for 5m.

maya: action items: sam — roll back canary to last known-good if patch takes longer than 2 hours. liam — open PR with TTL+confirm+escape. anya — run synthetic repro in region 3 to validate compile queue behavior.

sam: rolled back canary now to previous revision. monitoring — compile-queue depth dropping.

infra-bot: Info: compile-queue depth = 42 (was 218).

maya: nice. keep an eye on autoscaler; if we get reintroduced load we may still need temporary scaling. Also capture traces for a few failing requests and attach to the PR.

liam: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4312 — contains tests + perf run in CI. will request urgent review.

anya: running repro rig in region 3 (#repro-job-77). will post results in 20m.

sam: FYI — added a temporary metric: kernel_switch_rate per op-shape. on the bad canary it was ~14 switches/min, baseline 0.6/min.

maya: excellent. let's keep this thread for status. thanks all. :thumbsup:
